source: User decisions of 2026-10-10 (SPEC.md, 'Decisions taken by the user' #1) and the v1 release post-mortem: initial frame needs at least one identifiable target, terminal frame needs both, reject only genuinely invalid tasks, RL/SFT/QA admitted by their own information needs while sharing task identity, version and split.

statuses.ADMIT: Admitted into this modality of the release.
statuses.HOLD: Task definition is valid but this candidate is not admitted in this round. Recoverable by re-review, re-rendering, or regenerating the initial state / endpoint for the same object pair. Not blacklisted. QA derived from a HOLD task stays admissible.
statuses.REJECT: Candidate (or item) is invalid and is never admitted in this version. A 'task_invalid:*' reason invalidates the task definition itself: it blocks RL, SFT and every QA item of the task and blacklists the object or pair for regeneration.

task_invalid:wrong_object.description: The outlined object is not the labelled category.

task_invalid:box_misaligned.description: Projected 3D box does not sit on the named object (label/box misaligned), seen in the terminal frame or in at least min_frames frames.

task_invalid:referring_ambiguous.description: The referring expression could equally denote another object visible in the image.

task_invalid:task_impossible.description: The goal cannot be satisfied in this scene.

precheck:*.description: Geometric pre-check failed before rendering (illegal pose/transition, certificate does not succeed, initial already successful, identifiability rules fail geometrically).

render_artifact_initial.description: Rendering defect in the initial frame.

render_artifact_terminal.description: Rendering defect in the terminal frame.

runtime_replay_failed.description: Runtime replay of the certificate did not reach canonical success.

initial_no_identifiable_target.description: No target identifiable in the initial frame.

terminal_target_not_identifiable.description: A target is not identifiable in the terminal frame.

terminal_target_not_hidden.description: occlusion_alignment only: in the terminal frame the reviewer does not see the target hidden behind the occluder (the occluder's box over-states what it covers, e.g. open furniture), so this target/occluder pair is not usable.

review_missing.description: Initial/terminal frame or task-level review absent.

review_invalid.description: Review does not follow the review schema.

review_uncertain.description: Reviewer left a required field null.

replay_missing.description: Runtime replay evidence required by policy but absent.

sft_render_artifact_turn_frame.description: A frame shown in an SFT user turn has a rendering defect.

sft_turn_frame_unreviewed.description: A frame shown in an SFT user turn was not reviewed.

sft_turn_frame_no_identifiable_target.description: Fewer identifiable targets than sft.turn_frame_min_identifiable in a turn frame.

sft_frame_missing_image.description: A frame needed by the conversation has no rendered image.

qa_render_artifact.description: QA state frame has a rendering defect.

qa_target_not_identifiable.description: An object the question refers to is not identifiable in this frame.

qa_box_misaligned_in_frame.description: Box misaligned for a referenced object in this frame (not enough to invalidate the task).

qa_invalid_label.description: Generator did not produce a valid label.

Round 10 used style continue (the blocked attempt, then the old shortest path), share 0.2, seed 20261015.
export.note_round10: 2026-10-15: the system prompt lists the env's real reward terms (reward_text actual with the S0 settings; blocked moves never end the episode) and a pose value that rounds to zero prints as 0.00, matching configs/rl_env_v10_S0.yaml; rounds 6-9 exported the legacy text and -0.00.

reviewer_rubric: You are auditing rendered frames from an indoor camera-navigation task. You REPORT what you see; you do not decide whether the task is kept.
Targets are outlined in the review copy of each frame: target A in RED, target B in BLUE (C in GREEN, D in YELLOW if present).
Task goal shown to the agent: "{goal}"
For EVERY frame listed below, fill in:

render_ok: false ONLY for a rendering defect that would mislead a viewer: large black or empty regions, smeared or floating blobs, torn or missing geometry, a mostly blank image. Ordinary blur, low texture or dim light is fine (true).

targets_identifiable[slot]: true if a person who reads the description (not the outline) could point to the correct object in this frame. A target that is partly cut off by the image border or partly hidden behind something is STILL identifiable when enough of it remains to recognise it. false if it is outside the view, hidden, too small, or cannot be told apart from similar objects. Use null only if you truly cannot judge.

box_alignment_ok[slot]: true if the outline sits on the described object; false if it is clearly on a different object, on empty space, or covers well under half of the object; null if the target is not in view in this frame.
notes: one short sentence for anything unusual (optional).
Then fill in once for the whole task (judge on the frame where both targets are best visible, usually the final frame):
label_matches[slot]: false if the outlined object is not of the named category ({categories}), i.e. the outline marks the wrong object.
referring_unambiguous[slot]: false if the description could equally refer to another object visible in these frames.
task_possible: false only if the goal clearly cannot be satisfied in this scene (for example the required view is blocked by a wall).

Important: it is EXPECTED that in the first frame one target is cropped, occluded or outside the view. Do not mark render_ok or box_alignment_ok false for that reason; just report targets_identifiable honestly.
Answer with JSON only, exactly in this shape: {schema}
hidden_target_rubric: Special rule for this task: the goal is to hide target {hidden} behind target {occluder}. In the final frame ({terminal}) target {hidden} is EXPECTED to be hidden.

In frame {terminal} the {hidden_color} outline is drawn where target {hidden} is, behind target {occluder} ({occluder_color} outline). Report targets_identifiable[{hidden}] honestly there (false is expected) and do not mark box_alignment_ok[{hidden}] false just because the object inside the {hidden_color} outline is covered.

Also fill target_hidden_by_occluder for frame {terminal}: true if the area inside the {hidden_color} outline lies inside the image and shows target {occluder} (or nothing of target {hidden}) because {occluder} covers it; false if target {hidden} is clearly visible, if the {hidden_color} outline is outside the image, or if nothing in front of it covers it; null only if you cannot judge.
